- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot early in upward trends.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.30) — model fails to capture sharp downside reversals.
- Lag in price corrections: model often delays mean reversion, especially after strong sentiment shifts (e.g., sentiment spikes from -0.40 to +0.70).
- Overshoot after spikes: model overreacts to sentiment-driven spikes, leading to exaggerated price peaks that don’t materialize.
- Mean reversion bias: model underestimates downward correction after prolonged upward runs (e.g., 3+ consecutive days above 75).
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts overestimate volatility in low-sentiment periods — model assumes momentum persists where sentiment weakens.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.20, reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for overconfidence; if sentiment < -0.30, increase forecast by 5–10% to compensate for underreaction.
